παρασκευάζω.d: I prepare; mid: I prepare, make preparations.

ὀθόνη.d: a linen cloth, a sheet, sail.

ἑρπετόν.d: a creeping creature, reptile, especially a serpent.

μηδαμῶς.g: by no means, not at all
μηδαμῶς.d: by no means, not at all.

εἰσκαλέομαι.d: I call in (to my house), invite.

ἀλλόφυλος.d: foreign, of another tribe or race.

εὐεργετέω.d: I do good deeds, perform kind service, benefit.

ἐπιμένω.d: (a) I remain, tarry, (b) I remain in, persist in.

ἀκροβυστία.d: (a technical word of Jewish use) foreskin, prepuce: used sometimes as a slang term by Jews, of Gentiles.

Φοινίκη.d: Phoenicia, a northern coast strip of the Roman province Syria.

Ἀντιόχεια.d: Antioch, (a) Antioch on the river Orontes, capital of the Province Syria, (b) "Pisidian" Antioch, not in Pisidia, but near Pisidia, in the Roman Province Galatia.

Κλαύδιος.d: (a) Claudius, the fourth of the Roman Emperors, Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, who ruled A.D. 41-54, (b) Claudius Lysias, a tribune at Jerusalem.

εὐπορέομαι.d: I have means, am prosperous, enjoy plenty.

τετράδιον.d: a quaternion, a group of four soldiers.

ἐκπίπτω.g: I fall out, fall off, fall away, fade away, wither away
ἐκπίπτω.d: I fall out, fall off, fall away; hence in nautical language: I fall off from the straight course; of flowers: I fade away, wither away; I fall from, lose, forfeit; I am cast ashore; I am fruitless.

Μᾶρκος.d: Mark, who also had the Hebrew name John, son of Mary, nephew of Barnabas, coadjutor of Barnabas, Paul, and Peter.

Ῥόδη.d: Rhoda, a maidservant in the house of John Mark's mother at Jerusalem.

κατασείω.d: I shake (the hand) up and down, wave; intrans: I beckon for silence.

θυμομαχέω.d: (lit: I fight desperately, hence) I am furiously angry with.

Τύριος.d: a Tyrian, an inhabitant of Tyre.

Βλάστος.d: Blastus, chamberlain of King Herod Agrippa I.

δημηγορέω.g: I make a public speech, address a multitude
δημηγορέω.d: I make a public speech, address a multitude.

δῆμος.d: properly: the people, especially citizens of a Greek city in popular assembly, but in NT, multitude, rabble.

συμπαραλαμβάνω.g: I take along as a companion
συμπαραλαμβάνω.d: I take along as a companion.

Λούκιος.d: Lucius, (a) of Cyrene, an early Christian, in the church of Antioch, by some identified with the evangelist Luke, (b) a Christian with Paul at Corinth, by some identified with (a).

Μαναήν.d: (Graecized form of Aramaic Menahem), Manaen, probably a member of Herod Antipas' court.

σύντροφος.d: one brought up with, a foster brother, an intimate friend.

λειτουργέω.d: I act in the public service, render service, minister, in the widest sense, of some special public religious service, but also of the service of priests and Levites.

Σελεύκεια.d: Seleucia, on the Syrian coast, the harbor of Syrian Antioch.

Σαλαμίς.d: Salamis, a city at the eastern end of Cyprus.

Πάφος.d: Paphos, a city at the western end of Cyprus.

Βαριησοῦς.d: Bar-Jesus, the name of the magician and false prophet at Paphos in Cyprus; he is also called Elymas.

Σέργιος.d: Sergius, the middle (gentile) name of the proconsul of Cyprus.

Ἐλύμας.d: Elymas, the name of the sorcerer at Paphos.

χειραγωγός.g: one who leads a helpless person by the hand
χειραγωγός.d: one who leads a helpless person by the hand.

Πέργη.d: Perga, a city on the river Cestrus in the Roman province Pamphylia.

Πισιδία.d: Pisidia, a country of Asia Minor, being the south-western part of the Roman province Galatia.

ἀνάγνωσις.d: recognition, reading; public reading (of the law and prophets in synagogue or church).

παροικία.d: a sojourning, a dwelling in a strange land.

τροποφορέω.d: I endure the ways of, put up with.

κατακληρονομέω.d: I give as an inheritance, distribute by lot.

Βενιαμίν.d: Benjamin, youngest son of Jacob, founder of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.

προκηρύσσω.d: I announce or preach beforehand, announce by herald.

ἐκπληρόω.g: I fill completely, fulfill in every particular
ἐκπληρόω.d: I fill completely, fulfill in every particular (to the utmost), make good.

ἔξειμι.d: (originally: I shall go out), I go out (away), depart.

παροτρύνω.d: I stir up, incite, urge on.

Ἰκόνιον.d: Iconium, a Phrygian city of the Roman province Galatia (modern Konia).

καταφεύγω.d: I flee for refuge (implying that the refuge is reached); aor. indicates moment of arrival.

Λυκαονία.d: Lycaonia, the country of the Lykaones, a district of Asia Minor, comprised within the Roman province Galatia and including the cities of Derbe and Lystra.

Λύστρα.c: Λύστρα, τά, dat. Λύστροις / Λύστρα, ἡ, acc. Λύστραν
Λύστρα.d: Lystra, a Lycaonian city in the southern part of the Roman province Galatia.

Δέρβη.d: Derbe, a town in Lycaonia and in the southern part of the Roman province Galatia.

Ζεύς.d: Zeus, the Greek god of the sky in all its manifestations, corresponding to the Roman Jupiter and to the leading god of the native Lycaonians.

Ἑρμῆς.d: (a) Hermes, the messenger and herald of the Greek gods, or rather the corresponding Lycaonian deity, (b) Hermes, a Roman Christian.

ὁμοιοπαθής.d: of like feelings, having similar passions and feelings, of like infirmities.

μάταιος.d: vain, unreal, ineffectual, unproductive; practically: godless.

ἀγαθουργέω.d: I work that which is good, perform good deeds.

καταπαύω.d: (a) trans: I cause to rest, bring to rest; I cause to refrain, (b) intrans: I rest.

ἐπιστηρίζω.d: I prop up, uphold, support, confirm, make stronger.

ἐμμένω.g: I remain or abide in, abide by, maintain
ἐμμένω.d: I remain (abide) in, abide by, maintain, persevere in.

χειροτονέω.d: I elect by show of hands, choose by vote, appoint.

Ἀττάλεια.d: Attalia, the port of Perga in Pamphylia.

ζήτημα.d: a question, subject of inquiry, dispute.

προπέμπω.d: I send forward, accompany, equip for a journey.

ἀνοικοδομέω.d: I rebuild, build up (what has fallen or been razed to the ground), sometimes merely: I build.

κατασκάπτω.d: I dig down under, demolish, undermine.

κατάλοιπος.d: left behind; the rest, the remainder.

παρενοχλέω.d: I trouble, cause disturbance to, annoy, harass.

ἐπιστέλλω.g: I write, send by letter to.
ἐπιστέλλω.d: I write, send by letter to.

ἀλίσγημα.d: pollution, perhaps a polluted thing (especially of food).

πνικτός.d: strangled (i.e. killed without letting out the blood).

Σίλας.d: Silas, a pet-form of the name "Silvanus"; a Roman citizen and a helper of Paul.

ἀνασκευάζω.d: I pervert, subvert, dismantle, unsettle, overthrow, destroy.

εἰδωλόθυτον.d: (of meat), sacrificed to an image (or an idol).

ῥώννυμαι.d: I strengthen, render firm; imperative at the end of letters: farewell.

Σιλᾶς.d: Silas, a pet-form of the name "Silvanus"; a Roman citizen and a helper of Paul.

ἀποχωρίζομαι.d: I separate from; mid: I part; pass: I am swept aside.

ἐκπλέω.d: I sail out (of harbor), sail away.

καταντάω.g: I come down, arrive at, reach
καταντάω.d: (a) I come down, either from high land to lower (or actually to the sea-coast), or from the high seas to the coast; hence met: I arrive at, reach (my destination), (b) of property: I come down (descend) by inheritance to an heir.

Τιμόθεος.d: Timothy, a Christian of Lystra, helper of Paul.

Γαλατικός.d: Galatic, belonging to the province Galatia.

Μυσία.d: Mysia, a country in the north-west of the Roman province Asia (and of Asia Minor).

Βιθυνία.d: Bithynia, a Roman province, north-west of Asia Minor and south-west of the Black Sea.

Τρῳάς.d: Troas, a harbor city of Mysia.

Μακεδών.d: a Macedonian, an inhabitant of the Roman province Macedonia.

Μακεδονία.d: (Hebrew), Macedonia, a Roman province north of Achaia (Greece).

Σαμοθρᾴκη.d: Samothrace, an island south of the province of Thrace.

Φίλιπποι.d: Philippi, a great city of the Roman province Macedonia.

κολωνία.d: a colony, a city settlement of Roman (soldier) citizens; a garrison city.

Λυδία.d: Lydia, a lady resident of Philippi, native of Thyatira in Lydia (Asia Minor), and engaged in the clothing trade.

πορφυρόπωλις.g: a female seller of purple cloth
πορφυρόπωλις.d: a female seller of purple cloth.

Θυάτειρα.d: Thyatira, a city of the old district Lydia, in the Roman province Asia.

πύθων.d: a divining spirit, Python, called after the Pythian serpent said to have guarded the oracle at Delphi and been slain by Apollo.

μαντεύομαι.d: I divine, practice soothsaying, suggesting the fraud involved in the practice.

περιρήγνυμι.d: I tear off, as of garments.

δεσμοφύλαξ.g: a keeper of a prison, a jailer
δεσμοφύλαξ.d: a keeper of a prison, a jailer.

ἐσώτερος.d: inner; with the article: the part that is within.

ἐπακροάομαι.d: I listen to, hear, hearken to.

θεμέλιον.d: (properly, an adj: belonging to the foundation), a foundation stone.

ἀνίημι.g: I let go, loosen, release, give up, neglect
ἀνίημι.d: I send up, produce, send back; I let go; I relax, loosen, hence met: I give up, desist from.

πανοικεί.g: with one's whole household or family
πανοικεί.d: with one's whole household or family.

ῥαβδοῦχος.d: a holder of the rods, a lictor, Roman officer, judge.

Ἀμφίπολις.d: Amphipolis, a leading city of Macedonia.

Θεσσαλονίκη.d: Thessalonica (modern Saloniki), an important city of the Roman province Macedonia.

προσκληρόομαι.d: I assign by lot, allot, associate with, follow as a disciple.

ἀγοραῖος.d: a lounger in the market-place, perhaps with the idea of agitator.

ὀχλοποιέω.d: I gather a crowd, make a riot.

Ἰάσων.d: Jason, a Christian of Thessalonica, perhaps the same as the "relative" of Paul.

πολιτάρχης.d: a ruler of a city, city magistrate.

ἀναστατόω.g: I turn upside down, upset, unsettle
ἀναστατόω.d: (perhaps a political metaphor), I turn upside down, upset, unsettle.

Βέροια.d: Berea, a town of the province Macedonia.

Ἀθῆναι.d: Athens, the intellectual capital of Greece.

κατείδωλος.d: full of images of idols, grossly idolatrous.

παρατυγχάνω.d: I come by chance, chance to meet.

Ἐπικούρειος.d: an Epicurean, one who holds the tenets of Epicurus.

σπερμολόγος.d: a babbler, gossiper, one who picks up seeds and trifles as does a bird.

δεισιδαίμων.g: respectful of what is divine, religious
δεισιδαίμων.d: respectful of what is divine; religious, perhaps, rather than superstitious (the usual meaning).

ἀναθεωρέω.d: I look at attentively, gaze at, consider.

σέβασμα.d: an object of worship or veneration.

βωμός.d: an altar, platform; a slightly-elevated spot.

εὐσεβέω.d: I am dutiful, pious, show piety towards, worship.

ἀνθρώπινος.d: belonging to human beings (especially as contrasted with God), human (as contrasted with divine).

προσδέομαι.d: I want more, need in addition.

ὁροθεσία.g: a setting of boundaries, definite limit
ὁροθεσία.d: a setting of boundaries, definite limit; plur: bounds.

ποιητής.d: (a) a "maker," poet, (b) a doer, carrier out, performer.

ὑπεροράω.d: I overlook, take no notice of, disregard.

Ἀρεοπαγίτης.g: member of the Council of the Areopagus
Ἀρεοπαγίτης.d: member of the Council of the Areopagus, an Areopagite.

Κόρινθος.d: Corinth, in north-east Peloponnese, the capital of the Roman province Achaia.

Ἀκύλας.d: the Greek way of writing the Latin Aquila, a male proper name; the husband of Priscilla (Prisca), and a Jew, of a family belonging to (Sinope in ?) Pontus.

Πρίσκιλλα.d: Prisca, Priscilla, the former being the more correct and formal name, the latter a diminutive and more familiar; a Roman lady, probably of good birth, wife of the Jewish Christian Aquila.

Ῥώμη.d: Rome, the famous city on the Tiber, the capital of the Roman Empire.

ὁμότεχνος.g: of the same trade or craft
ὁμότεχνος.d: of the same trade or craft.

ἀντιτάσσομαι.d: I set myself against, resist (the attack of).

συνομορέω.d: I am contiguous with, am next door to.

Κρίσπος.d: Crispus, ruler of the synagogue at Corinth, converted and baptized by Paul.

Γαλλίων.d: Gallio, Lucius Iunius Gallio, who received this name by adoption into another family, but was born brother of the philosopher Seneca and originally named L. Annaeus Nouatus; proconsul of the Roman province Achaia from spring A.D. 52 to spring 53.

Ἀχαΐα.d: the Roman Province Achaia, governed by a proconsul, and practically conterminous with modern Greece before 1912.

κατεφίστημι.d: I rush, assault, rise up against.

ἀναπείθω.g: I urge by evil persuasion, I tempt

ἀδίκημα.d: a legal wrong, crime (with which one is charged), misdeed, crime against God, a sin.

ῥᾳδιούργημα.d: a careless action, an act of villainy.

Σωσθένης.d: Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue at Corinth.

Κεγχρεαί.d: Cenchreae, the port of Corinth on the Saronic Gulf.

εὐχή.d: a prayer comprising a vow; a prayer, vow.

Ἔφεσος.d: Ephesus, a coast city, capital of the Roman province Asia.

ἐπινεύω.d: I nod to, assent to, consent.

ζέω.d: (lit: I boil, am boiling), I burn (in spirit), am fervent.

σκληρύνω.d: I harden, make hard, make stubborn.

σχολή.d: leisure, a school, place where there is leisure.

Τύραννος.d: Tyrannus, an inhabitant of Ephesus, probably a rhetorician.

χρώς.d: the skin, surface of the body.

περιέρχομαι.g: I move about, make a circuit, tack
περιέρχομαι.d: I go around, move about, visit; I make a circuit, tack (as a ship).

ἐξορκιστής.d: an exorcist, a caster out of evil spirits by the use of names or spells.

περίεργος.d: of persons: over-careful; curious, meddling, a busy-body; of things: over-wrought; superfluous; curious, uncanny; subst: curious arts, magic.

συμψηφίζω.d: I compute, reckon up, count together.

Ἔραστος.d: Erastus, steward of Corinth, a Christian.

Ἄρτεμις.d: Artemis, a goddess, worshipped principally at Ephesus, typifying fertility (she had no relation with the other Artemis, the maiden huntress, to whom corresponded the Latin Diana).

θέατρον.d: (a) a theatre, a semi-circular stone building, generally open to the sky, (b) a spectacle, show.

Γάϊος.d: Gaius, (a) a Corinthian, (b) a Macedonian, (c) a citizen of Derbe, (d) an Ephesian.

Ἀρίσταρχος.d: Aristarchus, a Christian, belonging to Thessalonica in Macedonia.

Ἀσιάρχης.d: an Asiarch, an official connected with the worship of Rome and the Emperor in the Roman province Asia.

καταστέλλω.d: I let down, lower; I keep down, restrain, pacify.

ἀναντίρρητος.d: indisputable, undeniable, not to be contradicted.

ἱερόσυλος.d: robbing temples, but possibly simply: sacrilegious.

ἐγκαλέω.g: I bring a charge against, accuse
ἐγκαλέω.d: I bring a charge against, accuse.

ἔννομος.d: (a) legal, statutory, duly constituted, (b) under the law, obedient to the law.

συστροφή.d: a gathering together, riotous concourse, conspiracy.

Ἑλλάς.d: Hellas, the native name for Greece.

Ἀσιανός.g: belonging to the Roman province Asia
Ἀσιανός.d: belonging to the Roman province Asia.

Τυχικός.d: Tychicus, a Christian of the Roman province Asia.

Τρόφιμος.d: Trophimus, a Christian of Ephesus in Asia.

Εὔτυχος.d: Eutychus, a young hearer of Paul at Troas.

καταφέρω.d: I bear down, overpower; I give a vote or verdict, bring charges.

τρίστεγον.g: having three stories, the third story
τρίστεγον.d: having three stories; subst: the third story.

Ἆσσος.d: Assos, a port of Mysia, in the Roman province Asia.

πεζεύω.d: I travel on foot, by land.

Μιτυλήνη.d: Mitylene, the capital of the island of Lesbos in the northern Aegean sea.

ἄντικρυς.d: right opposite, off (nautical sense), over against.

Χίος.d: Chios (modern Scio), an important island in the Aegean Sea, off the west central coast of Asia Minor.

Σάμος.d: Samos, an island in the Aegean sea off the coast of Asia Minor, near Ephesus and Miletus.

Μίλητος.d: Miletus, a city on the coast of the Roman province Asia.

χρονοτριβέω.d: I waste time, spend time, delay.

ὑποστέλλω.d: I withdraw, draw back, keep back, shun, conceal.

μαρτύρομαι.g: I call to witness, testify, solemnly charge
μαρτύρομαι.d: (properly: I call (summon) to witness, and then absolutely) I testify, protest, asseverate; I conjure, solemnly charge.

ἐπίσκοπος.d: (used as an official title in civil life), overseer, supervisor, ruler, especially used with reference to the supervising function exercised by an elder or presbyter of a church or congregation.

Κώς.d: Cos, an island in the Aegean Sea, south-west of Asia Minor.

Ῥόδος.d: Rhodes, an island in the Aegean sea, south-west of Asia Minor.

Πάταρα.d: Patara, a town on the coast of the Roman province Lycia.

ἐξαρτίζω.d: (a) I fit up, completely furnish, equip, furnish, supply, (b) I accomplish, finish.

Πτολεμαΐς.d: Ptolemais, a coast city of Phoenicia, midway between Tyre and Caesarea.

εὐαγγελιστής.g: an evangelist, bearer of good tidings
εὐαγγελιστής.d: an evangelist, a missionary, bearer of good tidings.

ἐντόπιος.g: belonging to the place, native, resident
ἐντόπιος.d: belonging to the place, native, resident; subst: a citizen.

συνθρύπτω.g: I break in pieces, crush, thoroughly weaken
συνθρύπτω.d: I break in pieces, crush, thoroughly weaken.

Μνάσων.d: Mnason, an early Christian, native of Cyprus, resident at a place between Caesarea and Jerusalem.

ξυράομαι.d: I shave, shear, cut off the hair.

ἀσφαλής.d: (lit: unfailing), safe, reliable, trustworthy, certain, sure.

παρεμβολή.g: a camp, barracks, army in battle array
παρεμβολή.d: a camp, fort, castle, barracks, army in battle array.

ἀναβαθμός.g: a step, a flight of steps
ἀναβαθμός.d: a step, a flight of steps; the well-known "stairs" leading up from the temple to the tower of Antonia at Jerusalem.

σικάριος.d: an assassin, murderer, bandit; one of the Sicarii.

Ἑβραΐς.d: the Hebrew language, or rather: Aramaic.

νυνί.d: adv. (a) of time: just now, even now; just at hand, immediately, (b) of logical connection: now then, (c) in commands and appeals: at this instant.

ἀπολογία.d: a verbal defense (particularly in a law court).

ἀκρίβεια.d: strictness, accuracy, exactness, attention to detail, scrupulousness.

ἀπολούομαι.d: I wash off, mid: I wash away (my sins, in baptism).

καθήκω.d: I come down, come to; I am unfit, proper.

ἀήρ.d: air, the lower air we breathe.

ἀνετάζω.d: I examine (a person on trial, a witness) judicially (frequently by the aid of torture).

προτείνω.d: I stretch out, tie up (for scourging), extend before.

κεφάλαιον.g: the chief matter, a sum of money
κεφάλαιον.d: (a) the chief matter, the main point, (b) a sum of money.

πολιτεία.d: (a) commonwealth, polity; citizen body, (b) (the Roman) citizenship, citizen-rights, franchise.

πολιτεύομαι.g: I live the life of a citizen
πολιτεύομαι.d: I live the life of a citizen, live.

ἱππεύς.d: a horse-soldier, a mounted soldier, a cavalryman.

δεξιολάβος.g: one posted on the right hand, a spear-man
δεξιολάβος.d: one posted on the right hand, a spear-man.

Φῆλιξ.d: Felix, third name of (Marcus) Antonius Felix, procurator of the Roman province Judea from an uncertain date (before A.D. 52 ?) till A.D. 59.

Λυσίας.d: Claudius Lysias, a Roman tribune of the soldiers in Jerusalem.

Ἀντιπατρίς.d: Antipatris, a town, where was a Roman colony, on the road between Caesarea and Jerusalem.

ἀναδίδωμι.g: I send up, deliver, hand over
ἀναδίδωμι.d: I send up, deliver, hand over, yield.

διακούω.g: I hear throughout, of a judicial hearing
διακούω.d: I hear throughout, of a judicial hearing.

Τέρτυλλος.d: Tertullus, a barrister acting as professional prosecutor of Paul at Caesarea.

εὐχαριστία.d: thankfulness, gratitude; giving of thanks, thanksgiving.

πρωτοστάτης.d: one who stands in the front rank, hence: a leader, ringleader, chief.

ἀπρόσκοπος.g: not offending, not causing offence, blameless
ἀπρόσκοπος.d: (free from hurt or harm, hence) not offending, not causing offence, blameless.

ἀναβάλλομαι.d: I postpone, defer, especially: I postpone the trial of.

Δρούσιλλα.d: Drusilla (born A.D. 39), daughter of Herod Agrippa I.

διετία.d: a period of two years, two years; according to ancient practice this means any period between one and two years.

Πόρκιος.d: Porcius, the middle (gentile) name of the procurator Festus.

κατατίθημι.d: (a) I lay down, deposit, (b) mid: I lay down or deposit a favor, with the view of receiving one in return, seek favor.

Βερνίκη.d: Bernice, daughter of Agrippa I and Kypros, and sister of M. Julius Agrippa II.

ἀνατίθεμαι.g: I lay a case before, impart, communicate, relate
ἀνατίθεμαι.d: I lay (a case) before, impart, communicate, declare, relate (with a view to consulting).

δεισιδαιμονία.d: religion in general; in a bad sense: superstition.

Σεβαστός.d: (official Greek equivalent of Augustus), venerated, august, a title of the Roman emperors; hence secondarily: Augustan, imperial.

διάγνωσις.d: judicial examination, decision; an act of discernment.

ἀκροατήριον.d: auditorium, recitation hall, court room (for hearing cases).

ἐντυγχάνω.g: I meet, encounter, call upon, make a petition
ἐντυγχάνω.d: (a) I meet, encounter, hence: (b) I call (upon), make a petition, make suit, supplication.

ἄλογος.d: without reason, irrational; contrary to reason, absurd.

θρησκεία.d: (underlying sense: reverence or worship of the gods), worship as expressed in ritual acts, religion.

ψῆφος.d: (a) a pebble, small stone, (b) hence, from their use in voting: a vote.

κέντρον.d: a sting, goad; met: of death.

σωφροσύνη.d: soundness of mind, sanity; self-control, sobriety.

ὁποῖος.d: of what kind or manner, of what sort.

Ἰούλιος.d: Julius, a Roman centurion on special service.

Ἀδραμυττηνός.d: belonging to Adramyttium, a port in Mysia, in Asia Minor.

χράομαι.g: I use, make use of, deal with
χράομαι.d: I use, make use of, deal with, take advantage of.

Μύρα.d: Myra, a port in Lycia, south-west Asia Minor.
